chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Three are kept imprisoned permanently: the one who is detained after death (to pay his debt), the woman who apostatizes from Islam, and the thief after the cutting of his hand and foot.

key_terms.قَطْعِ الْيَدِ وَالرِّجْلِ: cutting of the hand and foot

ai.seo_question: Who are the three people kept in prison permanently according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) specifies three categories subject to permanent imprisonment (khalad), notably including the apostate woman, which highlights the distinct jurisprudential treatment of gender in Shia penal law. While the debtor and thief are mentioned, the inclusion of the apostate woman underscores the severity of her status compared to the male apostate, who is typically given a period for repentance before execution. This ruling is foundational in understanding the concept of indefinite detention for specific crimes where the primary punishment is not immediate execution.
